subject: Mid-Q check: OKR status, proposed scope trims, and evidence/dependency asks for QBR
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-10-02T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Mid-Q check: OKR status, proposed scope trims, and evidence/dependency asks for QBR

Hi all,

Quick mid-quarter pulse on the leadership-facing OKRs so we can lock what goes into the QBR deck next week and surface any exec decisions early. I ran the OPR dashboard and pulled the highlights into the attached QBR_prep_deck_v2.pptx. TL;DR: we can get to 70% of our stretch if we re-scope one initiative and get two infra/security commits.

Objective-level snapshot:
- Reduce inference p99 latency (OKR-1): current trend - 18% down from baseline, but p99 still misses SLO for peak traffic. Risk: continued p99 regressions if we push larger batch windows.
- Unit cost per 1k tokens (OKR-2): on track for base target, but stretch requiring quantization/auto-batching is blocked by infra rollout timeline.
- Private deployments uptime (OKR-3): 99.87% YTD; a final fix for the autoscaler bug would secure stretch but needs a 2-week dedicated infra window.

Proposed short re-scope (for QBR candid slide):
- Move OKR-2 stretch from "platform-wide auto-quantization" to "pilot with three customers (Acme Health + 2 others)" to reduce blast radius and unblock cost wins.
- For OKR-1, keep latency target but accept a phased rollout of batching (phase 1: 5ms median improvement w/o larger batch windows).

Dependencies / asks (what I need from this thread):
1) Vanessa: approval to present the pilot-based stretch (instead of platform-wide), and a green light to ask Sales & CS to pull two willing pilot customers into the slide.
2) Karthik: a 2-week infra window starting 2026-10-11 to fix the autoscaler regression and enable the quantization pilot. Also need a concrete ETA for kernel-level testing (can we commit to a test pass by 2026-10-16?).
3) Naomi: a one-page executive narrative for the QBR (due 2026-10-06 COB) that explains the risk->mitigation->ask for the latency and cost slides.
4) For the Acme procurement thread: procurement has asked for SOC2 evidence and environment separation details; we need to confirm what we can surface in the QBR timeline.

Attachments: QBR_prep_deck_v2.pptx (slides), I also exported a dependency tracker but will add it after Karthik confirms timelines.

What I will present at the prep sync if I don’t hear back by EOD Friday: the pilot-based stretch, and a request for a 2-week infra window. If any of you object, please flag now so I can adjust the deck.

Thanks —
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Head of Product Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-02T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mid-Q check: OKR status, proposed scope trims, and evidence/dependency asks for QBR

On Fri, Oct 2, 2026 at 9:15 AM Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com> wrote:
> Quick mid-quarter pulse on the leadership-facing OKRs so we can lock what goes into the QBR deck next week and surface any exec decisions early.

Thanks Rachel — good, pragmatic framing. I support the pilot approach for the cost stretch (makes the QBR narrative cleaner and gives Sales a concrete ask). Approvals below:
- Approve pilot-based stretch (Rachel: please add the measurable acceptance criteria for the pilot slide).
- Approve asking Sales/CS to recruit Acme and two additional pilots. I’ll loop in Marissa to nudge the CS leads.

Karthik — please confirm feasibility of the 2-week infra window starting 10/11 and whether the kernel test pass by 10/16 is realistic. If you need scope narrowed (e.g., only autoscaler fix first, quantization second), call that out — we can commit a phased infra plan.

Naomi — please send the one-pager by 10/06 COB; use the attached deck’s summary slide as a template.

Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Strategic Programs
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-02T15:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mid-Q check: OKR status, proposed scope trims, and evidence/dependency asks for QBR

On Fri, Oct 2, 2026 at 11:02 AM Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com> wrote:
> Karthik — please confirm feasibility of the 2-week infra window starting 10/11 and whether the kernel test pass by 10/16 is realistic.

We can take the 2-week window starting 2026-10-11 but need to scope the work to ensure no collateral risk to Dedicated pools. Proposed plan:
- Week 1 (10/11–10/15): dedicate 3 infra SREs to repro + fix autoscaler regression in staging, run canary deploys on a small fleet.
- Week 2 (10/18–10/22): expand canaries, run load testing across quantized variants.

Kernel-level testing: if we prioritize the autoscaler fix only (no kernel changes), I can guarantee a staging test pass by 10/16. If we include kernel/quantization changes, we need an extra week (test pass target 10/23).

I attached a short dependency_tracker.csv with the items I called out (owners, impact, ETA). If you want the autoscaler-only path for the QBR ask, we can call that out as a lower-risk exact ask to execs.

Karthik Iyer
Staff Engineer, Platform
Redwood Inference

Thanks Rachel — Acme is enthusiastic about participating as a pilot customer. Quick notes from procurement:
1) SOC2 evidence request — we can provide the standard evidence packet; target delivery: 2026-10-08. Please send the checklist of what you will include (network diagrams, retention policy, SOC2 bridge letter).
2) Environment separation: procurement says they need a one-page description of how customer workloads are isolated from shared pools and how data is retained.

If you can send the SOC2 checklist and the one-pager by 10/06, we’ll confirm the pilot agreement and provide a point-of-contact for CS.
